entries.title: Proverbs 5:1
segments:
. A warning against the seductive arts of wicked women, enforced by considering the advantages of chastity, and the miserable end of the wicked. 
 
    1. This connection of wisdom and understanding is frequent (
); the first denotes the use of wise means for wise ends; the other, the exercise of a proper discrimination in their discovery.

entries.title: Proverbs 5:2
segments:
2. regard--or, "observe." 
 
    keep--preserve constantly.

entries.title: Proverbs 5:3
segments: 3. (Compare

segments: 4. her end--literally, "her future," in sense of reward, what follows (compare
). Its nature is evinced by the use of figures, opposite those of
. The physical and moral suffering of the deluded profligate are notoriously terrible.

entries.title: Proverbs 5:5
segments: 5. feet ... , steps--that is, course of life ends in death.

entries.title: Proverbs 5:6
segments: 6. her ways ... know--Some prefer, "that she may not ponder the path of life," &c.; but perhaps a better sense is, "her ways are varied, so as to prevent your knowledge of her true character, and so of true happiness."

entries.title: Proverbs 5:8
segments: 8, 9. Avoid the slightest temptation.

entries.title: Proverbs 5:15
segments: 15-20. By figures, in which well, cistern, and fountain (
) represent the wife, and rivers of waters (
) the children, men are exhorted to constancy and satisfaction in lawful conjugal enjoyments. In
, fountains (in the plural) rather denote the produce or waters of a spring, literally, "what is from a spring," and corresponds with "rivers of waters."

entries.title: Proverbs 5:17
segments: 17. only thine own--harlots' children have no known father.

entries.title: Proverbs 5:18
segments: 18. wife ... youth--married in youth.
